title.narrative: Fostering resilience food security and social cohesion for communities affected by the Conflict in Sudan.

description.narrative: Objective: Strengthening resilience, restoring sustainable livelihoods and promoting peaceful coexistence in communities affected by the Sudan conflict in Sudan and across the border in South Sudan.Outcome 1: Enhanced food and nutrition security through climate-adaptive agriculture, and diversified livelihood options.Outcome 2: Strengthened individual and community capacities to prevent, mitigate and respond to Gender Based Violence (GBV), safety threats and conflict.Outcome 3: Improved access to basic services (WASH facilities and services in schools and health facilities) and community infrastructure.Outcome 4: Enhanced adaptation and mitigation capacities to climate-related disasters.

The project directly targets 42,504 (24,300 female, 18,204 male, incl. 3042 People with disabilities-PwD ) conflict-affected and highly vulnerable project participants in South Sudan, incl. women, girls, youth, PwD, returnees, IDPs, and smallholder farmers and pastoralists who face limited access to land, inputs, services, and safe livelihood opportunities. Women & girls benefit through strengthened protection systems, GBV prevention and response services, livelihood support, improved access to essential services, and enhanced participation in community structures. Youth gain from vocational training, business skills, market linkages and inclusion in peace and governance mechanisms. PwD benefit through accessible services, tailored livelihood support, and representation in local committees. Smallholder farmers and pastoralists directly benefit through climate-resilient production support, improved water access, input delivery systems, and market integration. Community committees (WUCs, CMDRR, peace, land governance structures) receive targeted technical and material support to manage resources transparently and inclusively. Local authorities benefit directly from capacity strengthening in climate-resilient agriculture, land governance, DRR, and coordination.255,469 (153,281 female, 102,188, incl. 25,547 PwD) indirect beneficiaries include entire host communities, who gain from improved infrastructure, reduced pressure on natural resources, strengthened conflict-sensitive governance, and more equitable service delivery. Local markets, traders, agro-dealers, and cooperatives benefit from stronger value chains and increased economic activity. Vulnerable households not directly enrolled in activities benefit from enhanced protection networks, functioning WASH services, reduced tensions, and more resilient local food systems. Ultimately, the broader population in the target counties benefits from strengthened social cohesion, improved stability, and reduced humanitarian dependence.

The proposed project aims to strengthen resilience and restore livelihoods while promoting peaceful coexistence for individuals affected by the Sudan conflict in both Sudan and South Sudan. By increasing food production and creating diversified income-generating opportunities, the project will enhance economic prospects for host communities and displaced populations in targeted areas. It will also focus on improving social integration and community cohesion, particularly by addressing the living conditions of women and girls and providing alternatives to violence for young men. Additionally, the project will invest in community-based infrastructure and assets that support livelihood activities, thereby fostering a more cohesive and resilient community.
